headline: A 2022 law requires the Copyright Office to waive certain copyright registration fees for works that win qualifying student competitions.
what_it_does: The law directs the Copyright Office to waive various copyright registration fees for works that win certain competitions. These are competitions sponsored by the Congressional Institute or established by Congress. To get the waiver, the registration application must be filed within a specified time frame. The Copyright Office may still waive fees for a qualifying work if the application is filed outside that time frame.

who_it_affects.group: Students whose artwork or other creative works win qualifying competitions
who_it_affects.how: They may register their winning works with the Copyright Office without paying the usual registration fees, if they file within the required time frame.
It must waive the specified fees for qualifying works and may waive them for late applications.

when_it_takes_effect: The act was enacted on October 17, 2022. The official summary does not give a separate effective date or the exact filing deadline.
